newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's faltering journey from communism.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's faltering journey from communism.

text.p: Following are the main political milestones since the end of one-party communist rule in Bulgaria, where parliamentary elections are to be held on Saturday.
November 1989 - Communist dictator Todor Zhivkov ousted by other senior party officials led by Foreign Minister Petar Mladenov, later to become president.
June 1990 - The former Communists, reformed as the Bulgarian Socialist Party, win sweeping victory in first democratic parliamentary elections.
July 1990 - Mladenov resigns as president, amid wave of anti-government protests.

August 1990 - Parliament elects former dissident and leader of anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) Zhelyu Zhelev as president. Zhelev later confirmed in post in 1992 full presidential elections.

December 1990 - Socialist-dominated parliament forms new coalition government, including some opposition members, after strikes and student unrest. Coalition approves tough reforms of state-controlled economy which remain mostly on paper.

October 1991 - UDF wins modest majority in parliament in early elections. Its government is ousted in no-confidence vote after only 11 months in power and replaced by non-party government backed by Socialists and ethnic Turkish party.
September 1994 - Government resigns amid accusations that it is delaying reforms.
December 1994 - Socialists win parliamentary majority in elections, but lose public support as economy deteriorates, inflation gathers pace and living standards plunge.
November 1996 - Presidential polls won by UDF's Petar Stoyanov.
December 1996 - Zhan Videnov resigns as prime minister and Socialist party leader.

January 1997 - Popular protests, led by the UDF, erupt against Socialist plans to form a new cabinet and complete full parliamentary term. Demonstrators besiege parliament, holding deputies prisoner for hours, and clash with police.

January-February 1997 - Nationwide rallies, marches and strikes by groups ranging from students to farmers and taxi drivers pile pressure on the Socialists to stand down. With no effective government to take essential economic measures, national currency goes into freefall.
February 1997 - President Stoyanov brokers agreement for early elections to be held in April. Interim cabinet formed.

March 1997 - IMF negotiates $657 million credit package with Bulgaria under conditions including the implementation of a strict monetary regime to shore up the battered lev currency, large-scale privatisations and other market reforms.
